title: The Harris 2019 layer-defined mouse hierarchy did not order IBL sound or click latencies of 32-35 cortical areas, but the same latency method recovered it for Allen visual flashes
abstract: Question: is the layer-defined cortico-thalamic hierarchy of Harris et al. 2019 a general temporal order of mouse cortex and thalamus, and do its feedforward/feedback (FF/FB) connection labels give the direction of sensory latency order that Knox net flow did not give? Data: IBL Brain-Wide Map region latencies to passive sound and valve clicks (from sci:bb0ad271), Harris hierarchy scores and labels, and, as a positive control, spikes of 12,631 Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels units (32 mice) to full-field flashes read with HTTP range requests. Method: a plan frozen before any hierarchy-latency statistic; Spearman rho of region latency and hierarchy score against 1,000 variogram-matched spatial surrogate maps; a connection-level concordance of FF/FB labels with latency order beside Knox net flow; a positive control with the same half-maximum latency method, added by a written amendment after the sound result. Results: the hierarchy did not order cortical latency to sound (rho 0.03, p 0.46, 32 areas) or valve clicks (rho 0.07, p 0.40, 35 areas); one-sided upper limits 0.47 and 0.45. Thalamic nuclei gave rho 0.02 (sound) and -0.29 (valve, reliable map, upper limit 0.10). FF/FB labels did not predict which region responded later (concordance 0.055, p 0.26; -0.003, p 0.52), and neither did Knox net flow. Partial, initial-hierarchy and split-half variants were also null. The positive control passed: flash latency rose along the hierarchy (rho 0.58 over 10 areas, p 0.046; 0.89 over six visual cortical areas, exact p 0.017; LGd 36 ms, VISp 41 ms, VISpm 55 ms). Most cortical areas responded to sound at about the same time (median 15.9 ms; anterior cingulate and retrosplenial areas as early as auditory cortex). Conclusion: in these data the hierarchy is a visual latency order, not a cortex-wide order for auditory input. Limitations: region-level tests with 15-35 regions exclude only strong relations; the cortical sound map had low between-area reliability (split-half 0.14); both IBL stimuli are auditory; the positive control uses other mice and mostly visual areas.
